chapter.name: Angles as Turns
chapter.names_note: Vary names across regions, religions and genders; use {{NAME_n}} tokens (n up to 10, one character = one token) and list them in name_slots.json; Keeko raises the wrong idea or a real-life link at the end of a concept video.

source: The Statue Game
Sahana stands on one spot facing the classroom door, with on

items.question: Sahana stands on one spot facing the classroom door, with one foot fixed. (a) She turns until she faces the door again. What turn is it? (b) She starts again and turns until her back is to the door. What turn is it?
steps: The start: Sahana faces the door.
(a): She turns and faces the door again. She is back at the starting position, so it is a full turn. Her free foot has drawn a complete circle.
(b): She turns until her back is to the door. She faces the opposite way, so it is a half turn. Her free foot has drawn a half-moon.
Check: a full turn ends where it began, and a half turn ends facing the other way.
items.answer: (a): a full turn; (b): a half turn

videos.answer: (a): a full turn; (b): a half turn

source: Statue Game: full turn and half turn

items.question: Can you recognise the child in the picture who has made a full turn? Who has made a half turn? How do you know? Discuss in class.
steps: In the first picture all four children face the front. That is the starting position.
A full turn brings a child back to the starting position, so the child faces the front again.
B and C face the front again, so B and C have made a full turn.
A half turn leaves a child facing the opposite way. A faces away from the front, so A has made a half turn.
D faces the side, so D has made neither a full turn nor a half turn.
Check: B and C face the same way as at the start, and A faces the opposite way.
items.answer: A made a half turn, because A faces the opposite way. B and C made a full turn, because they face the way they faced at the start.

videos.answer: A made a half turn, because A faces the opposite way. B and C made a full turn, because they face the way they faced at the start.

source: A seat on the giant wheel takes 1 half turn and then 2 quart

items.question: A seat on the giant wheel takes 1 half turn and then 2 quarter turns, all in the same direction. What turn is that in all?
steps: A half turn is 1/2 of a full turn. Two quarter turns are 2/4, which is 1/2.
1 is a full turn, so the seat is back at the starting position E.
Check: 1 half turn is 2 quarter turns, so the seat made 2 + 2 = 4 quarter turns, and 4 quarter turns make a full turn.
items.answer: A full turn, so the seat is back at E

videos.answer: A full turn, so the seat is back at E

source: Reema's Giant Wheel: two half turns

items.question: A giant wheel makes a full turn when it comes back to the starting position E. Reema takes two half turns in the same direction. It is like a ___ turn.
steps: A half turn is 1/2 of a full turn.
Two half turns in the same direction: 1/2 + 1/2 = 2/2 = 1.
1 is a full turn, so the seat is back at the starting position E.
Check: the first half turn takes the seat half way round and the second takes it the rest of the way.
items.answer: A full turn, because 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.

videos.answer: A full turn, because 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.

source: Reema's Giant Wheel: two quarter turns

items.question: A giant wheel makes a full turn when it comes back to the starting position E. What happens if Reema takes 2 quarter turns in the same direction? It is like a ___ turn.
steps: A quarter turn is 1/4 of a full turn.
Two quarter turns in the same direction: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4.
2/4 is the same as 1/2, because 2 ÷ 2 = 1 and 4 ÷ 2 = 2.
So two quarter turns are a half turn.
Check: two quarter turns take the seat half way round, and a half turn is half way round.
items.answer: A half turn, because 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

videos.answer: A half turn, because 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

source: Reema's Giant Wheel: four quarter turns

items.question: A giant wheel makes a full turn when it comes back to the starting position E. What happens if Reema takes 4 quarter turns in the same direction? It is like a ___ turn.
steps: Four quarter turns in the same direction: 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 4/4.
4/4 = 1, so it is a full turn.
The seat is back at the starting position E.
Check: two quarter turns make a half turn, and two half turns make a full turn, so four quarter turns make a full turn.
items.answer: A full turn, because 4/4 = 1.

videos.answer: A full turn, because 4/4 = 1.

source: Three practice hinges, P, Q and R, are opened as far as they

items.question: Three practice hinges, P, Q and R, are opened as far as they go (a practice picture). P opens exactly to the corner of a book. Q opens less than the corner. R opens wider than the corner. Compare the greatest turn of each with a quarter turn.
steps: The corner of a book is a quarter turn, so it is the guide.
P opens exactly to the corner: its greatest turn is a 1/4 turn.
Q opens less than the corner: its greatest turn is less than a 1/4 turn.
R opens wider than the corner: its greatest turn is more than a 1/4 turn.
Check: all three hinges were compared with the same guide, the corner of a book.
items.answer: P: a 1/4 turn; Q: less than a 1/4 turn; R: more than a 1/4 turn

videos.answer: P: a 1/4 turn; Q: less than a 1/4 turn; R: more than a 1/4 turn

source: Everyday Turns: objects that turn

items.question: Write some of the everyday objects that involve turns. For example, taps, ___, ___, ___, ___, and ___.
steps: Think of things that turn on a spot or on a hinge.
From your maths book: a tap, a door on its hinge, a clothes clip, tongs, scissors, a file cover, a clock hand, a giant wheel, a lid, a nut.
Pick five of them to write after taps.
Check: each one swings or spins round a fixed point.
items.answer: Sample answer: door, scissors, clock hand, giant wheel, lid. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: door, scissors, clock hand, giant wheel, lid. Your answer may differ.

source: Everyday Turns: the greatest turn

items.question: What is the maximum possible turn in each of these cases? Check and tick: less than a 1/4 turn, 1/4 turn, or more than a 1/4 turn. (a): Clothes clip; (b): Door with hinge; (c): Tongs; (d): Scissors; (e): File cover
steps: Use a quarter turn, the corner of a book, as the guide. Open each object as far as it goes and compare.
(a): the clothes clip opens only a little, less than the corner: less than a 1/4 turn.
(b): the door with hinge swings wider than the corner: more than a 1/4 turn.
(c): the tongs open less than the corner: less than a 1/4 turn.
(d): the scissors open about to the corner: a 1/4 turn.
(e): the file cover opens wider than the corner, even flat: more than a 1/4 turn.
Check: these are sample ticks for common objects. Your own objects may differ a little, so check them with the corner of a book.
items.answer: Sample answer: (a): less than 1/4; (b): more than 1/4; (c): less than 1/4; (d): 1/4; (e): more than 1/4. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: (a): less than 1/4; (b): more than 1/4; (c): less than 1/4; (d): 1/4; (e): more than 1/4. Your answer may differ.

source: Everyday Turns: half turn objects

items.question: Do any of the objects in the table (clothes clip, door with hinge, tongs, scissors, file cover) make a half turn? Write their names.
steps: A half turn is two quarter turns, so the arm and the start lie in one straight line.
A door can swing open until it is flat against the wall: a half turn.
A file cover can open until it lies flat on the table: a half turn.
A clothes clip, tongs and scissors cannot open that far.
Check: only the objects that open flat make a half turn.
items.answer: Sample answer: the door with hinge and the file cover. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: the door with hinge and the file cover. Your answer may differ.

source: Everyday Turns: full turn objects

items.question: Do any of the objects in the table (clothes clip, door with hinge, tongs, scissors, file cover) make a full turn? Write their names.
steps: A full turn brings the object back to where it started.
A hinge stops when the door, the cover or the blades meet each other or the wall. It cannot go all the way round.
The clothes clip, the door, the tongs, the scissors and the file cover all stop before a full turn.
Check: none of the five turns round and round like a wheel.
items.answer: Sample answer: none of the five. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: none of the five. Your answer may differ.

source: Pragya opens her paper fan to three places. At X the two end

items.question: Pragya opens her paper fan to three places. At X the two end sticks make exactly a quarter turn. At Y they make a little less than a quarter turn. At Z they make more than a quarter turn but less than a half turn. Name the angle at X, at Y and at Z.
steps: The guide is a quarter turn, a square corner.
X is exactly a quarter turn: a right angle.
Y is less than a quarter turn: an acute angle.
Z is more than a quarter turn and less than a half turn: an obtuse angle.
Check: X, Y and Z were all compared with the same quarter turn.
items.answer: X: a right angle; Y: an acute angle; Z: an obtuse angle

videos.answer: X: a right angle; Y: an acute angle; Z: an obtuse angle

source: Pragya's paper fan opens by a half turn and then by one more

items.question: Pragya's paper fan opens by a half turn and then by one more quarter turn in the same direction. What turn is that in all, and how does it compare with a straight angle?
steps: A half turn is 1/2 and a quarter turn is 1/4. 1/2 is the same as 2/4.
A straight angle is a 1/2 turn, which is 2/4. 3/4 is more than 2/4.
So the turn is 3/4, more than a straight angle.
Check: 3 quarter turns are one quarter turn short of a full turn.
items.answer: A 3/4 turn, more than a straight angle

videos.answer: A 3/4 turn, more than a straight angle

source: Let Us Do (angles), (a)

items.question: Use your paper fan to show different acute angles and obtuse angles.
steps: Hold one stick of the fan still. This is the starting line.
Open the fan a little, less than a quarter turn: an acute angle.
Open it to a quarter turn, a square corner: a right angle.
Open it a bit more, more than a quarter turn but less than a half turn: an obtuse angle.
Check: each angle was compared with a quarter turn.
items.answer: Sample answer: less than a 1/4 turn is acute; between a 1/4 and a 1/2 turn is obtuse. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: less than a 1/4 turn is acute; between a 1/4 and a 1/2 turn is obtuse. Your answer may differ.

source: Let Us Do (angles), (a) two acute turns

items.question: Make an acute turn with the straws or fan. Continue to make another acute turn. Can the two acute turns together make another acute turn?
steps: An acute turn is less than a quarter turn.
Make two small acute turns, one after the other. Together they can still be less than a quarter turn: acute.
Make two bigger turns that are each almost a quarter turn. Together they are more than a quarter turn, so the angle can be obtuse.
Two acute turns can also add up to exactly a quarter turn: a right angle.
So it depends on how big each turn is.
items.answer: Sometimes. Two small acute turns together can be acute; two bigger ones can make a right angle or an obtuse angle.

videos.answer: Sometimes. Two small acute turns together can be acute; two bigger ones can make a right angle or an obtuse angle.

source: Let Us Do (angles), (b)

items.question: You might have built houses using the hard covers of notebooks or cardboard pieces. Look at the angles marked in the house. What angles are you able to see in this house? Write your answers as right, acute or obtuse angle. A: ___; B: ___; C: ___; D: ___; E: ___; F: ___; G: ___; H: ___
steps: Compare each marked angle with a quarter turn, a square corner.
A: the roof books open wider than a square corner: obtuse.
B: a book standing on a flat book makes a square corner: right.
C: the two leaning books meet in a narrow point: acute.
D: the leaning book against the upright book is narrower than a square corner: acute.
E: the leaning book meets the upright book in a narrow angle: acute.
F: an upright book on the flat book: right.
G: an upright book on the flat book: right.
H: the leaning book meets the flat book in a wide angle: obtuse.
Check: 3 right angles, 3 acute angles and 2 obtuse angles make 3 + 3 + 2 = 8 angles, one for each letter.
items.answer: A: obtuse; B: right; C: acute; D: acute; E: acute; F: right; G: right; H: obtuse.

videos.answer: A: obtuse; B: right; C: acute; D: acute; E: acute; F: right; G: right; H: obtuse.

source: Let Us Do (angles), (c)

items.question: Make a 5-sided shape with 2 right angles, 2 obtuse angles, and 1 acute angle in your notebook.
steps: Use square paper. Start at the bottom left corner.
Draw a line 4 squares to the right, then a line 2 squares up.
Draw a slanting line 2 squares left and 4 squares up.
Draw a slanting line 2 squares left and 4 squares down.
Draw a line 2 squares down, back to the start. The shape has 5 sides.
The two bottom corners are right angles.
The two corners where the walls meet the roof are wider than a right angle: obtuse.
The top point is narrower than a right angle: acute.
Check: 2 right angles, 2 obtuse angles and 1 acute angle make 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 angles, one for each of the 5 sides.
items.answer: Sample answer: a house shape with 2 right angles, 2 obtuse angles and 1 acute angle. Your shape may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: a house shape with 2 right angles, 2 obtuse angles and 1 acute angle. Your shape may differ.

source: Let Us Do (angles), (d)

items.question: Look at the angle formation between the legs of these gymnasts. Identify whether the angles are acute, obtuse, right or straight.
steps: Compare each angle between the legs with a quarter turn.
Top picture: narrower than a square corner: acute.
Second picture: exactly a square corner: right.
Third picture: wider than a square corner but not a straight line: obtuse.
Fourth picture: wider still, nearly a straight line, but not straight: obtuse.
Fifth picture: the legs are in one straight line, a half turn: straight.
Check: the angles grow from picture to picture, from acute to straight.
items.answer: Top to bottom: acute, right, obtuse, obtuse, straight.

videos.answer: Top to bottom: acute, right, obtuse, obtuse, straight.

source: The straw on the circle with 8 equal parts turns 5 parts, an

items.question: The straw on the circle with 8 equal parts turns 5 parts, and then 2 more parts in the same direction. What turn is that, and how much more is needed for a full turn?
steps: Each part is a 1/8 turn.
5 parts and 2 more parts make 5 + 2 = 7 parts.
7 parts of the 8 make a 7/8 turn.
A full turn is 8 parts, and 8 − 7 = 1.
So 1 more part, a 1/8 turn, completes the full turn.
items.answer: A 7/8 turn; 1 more part, a 1/8 turn, makes a full turn

videos.answer: A 7/8 turn; 1 more part, a 1/8 turn, makes a full turn

source: How many 1/12 pieces cover a 1/6 piece, a 2/6 piece and a 3/

items.question: How many 1/12 pieces cover a 1/6 piece, a 2/6 piece and a 3/6 piece?
steps: A 1/12 piece is half of a 1/6 piece, so 2 pieces of 1/12 cover a 1/6 piece.
A 2/6 piece is 2 pieces of 1/6, so it needs 2 × 2 = 4 pieces of 1/12.
A 3/6 piece is 3 pieces of 1/6, so it needs 3 × 2 = 6 pieces of 1/12.
Check: 3/6 is the same as 1/2, and 6 pieces of 1/12 make 6/12 = 1/2.
items.answer: 2 pieces, 4 pieces and 6 pieces of 1/12

videos.answer: 2 pieces, 4 pieces and 6 pieces of 1/12

source: Angle Measuring Tool: show the turns

items.question: Show a 1/8 turn of the straw. Show a 2/8 turn. Show a 1/4 turn. Show a 3/8 turn.
steps: The circle is folded into 8 equal parts. Each part is a 1/8 turn.
A 1/8 turn is 1 part from the starting point A.
A 2/8 turn is 2 parts from A.
A 1/4 turn is the same as 2/8, because 8 ÷ 4 = 2 parts. So it is also 2 parts from A.
A 3/8 turn is 3 parts from A.
Check: 1/8, 2/8 and 3/8 move the straw 1, 2 and 3 parts, and 1/4 = 2/8 lands on the same place as 2/8.
items.answer: 1/8: 1 part; 2/8: 2 parts; 1/4: 2 parts, the same as 2/8; 3/8: 3 parts.

videos.answer: 1/8: 1 part; 2/8: 2 parts; 1/4: 2 parts, the same as 2/8; 3/8: 3 parts.

source: Angle Measuring Tool: eighths and a right angle

items.question: What angle have you made with a 2/8 turn? A 1/8 turn is half of a quarter turn.
steps: A 2/8 turn is 2 parts of the 8.
A 1/4 turn is a quarter turn, and a quarter turn makes a right angle.
Check: a 1/8 turn is half of a quarter turn, so two 1/8 turns make a quarter turn.
items.answer: A right angle, because 2/8 = 1/4 is a quarter turn.

videos.answer: A right angle, because 2/8 = 1/4 is a quarter turn.

source: Angle Measuring Tool: eighths and a straight angle

items.question: What angle have you made with a 4/8 turn?
steps: A 4/8 turn is 4 parts of the 8.
A 1/2 turn is a half turn, and a half turn makes a straight angle.
Check: 4/8 = 2/8 + 2/8 = 1/4 + 1/4, which is two quarter turns.
items.answer: A straight angle, because 4/8 = 1/2 is a half turn.

videos.answer: A straight angle, because 4/8 = 1/2 is a half turn.

source: Angle Measuring Tool: three-quarter turn and full turn

items.question: Continue turning by 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, and 8/8. Check when you have completed a 3/4 turn and a full turn.
steps: Keep turning the straw part by part: 5/8, 6/8, 7/8 and 8/8.
6/8 = 3/4, because 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So the straw has made a 3/4 turn at 6 parts.
At 8/8 the straw is back on the starting point A. 8/8 = 1, a full turn.
Check: 3/4 is 3 quarter turns, and 3 quarters plus 1 more quarter make 4 quarters, a full turn.
items.answer: 6/8 is the 3/4 turn; 8/8 is the full turn.

videos.answer: 6/8 is the 3/4 turn; 8/8 is the full turn.

source: Let Us Think: Q1

items.question: In the following circles, the end points of 1/2, 1/4, and 1/8 turns are shown. Draw arrows to show the starting points.
steps: The green dashed arrow in each circle goes the way the hands of a clock move. Each turn goes that way from the starting arrow to the red end arrow.
To find a starting arrow, turn back from the end arrow by the given part of a full turn.
1/2 turn: turning back half way gives the opposite arrow. End lower right gives start upper left. End upper right gives start lower left.
1/8 turn: turning back half of a quarter turn. End right gives start upper right. End lower right gives start right.
1/4 turn: turning back a quarter turn, a square corner. End upper left gives start lower left. End straight down gives start right.
Check: from each start, turn the given part the clock way and land on the red arrow.
items.answer: Top circle, then bottom circle. 1/2: upper left, lower left. 1/8: upper right, right. 1/4: lower left, right.

videos.answer: Top circle, then bottom circle. 1/2: upper left, lower left. 1/8: upper right, right. 1/4: lower left, right.

source: Angle Measuring Tool: turns in sixths

items.question: Show the turns of the straw equal to 1/6, 2/6, and so on until you complete a full circle.
steps: The circle is folded in half, then each half into 3 equal parts: 2 × 3 = 6 equal parts.
Each part is a 1/6 turn.
Turn the straw 1 part at a time from the starting point: 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6, 5/6, 6/6.
2/6 = 1/3 and 3/6 = 1/2, a half turn, a straight angle. 4/6 = 2/3.
At 6/6 the straw is back on the starting point: a full turn.
Check: 6 parts of 1/6 make 6/6 = 1.
items.answer: The straw turns 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6, 5/6 and 6/6; 6/6 is a full turn.

videos.answer: The straw turns 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6, 5/6 and 6/6; 6/6 is a full turn.

source: Angle Measuring Tool: half of one sixth

items.question: Can you guess what turn of the straw will be equal to half of a 1/6 turn?
steps: A 1/6 part is folded in half, so it is cut into 2 equal small parts.
The whole circle has 6 parts of 1/6, and each is cut into 2 small parts: 6 × 2 = 12 small parts.
So each small part is 1 of 12 equal parts: a 1/12 turn.
Check: 2 small parts make 2/12 = 1/6.
items.answer: A 1/12 turn.

videos.answer: A 1/12 turn.

source: An angle is covered exactly by one 1/6 piece and one 1/12 pi

items.question: An angle is covered exactly by one 1/6 piece and one 1/12 piece laid side by side. What turn does the angle make, and what kind of angle is it?
steps: Lay the 1/6 piece on the angle, starting from the first line, and the 1/12 piece next to it.
1/6 is 2 pieces of 1/12, so 1/6 = 2/12.
A 1/4 turn is a right angle.
Check: 3 pieces of 1/12 make a quarter turn, and 12 pieces make a full turn.
items.answer: A 1/4 turn: a right angle

videos.answer: A 1/4 turn: a right angle

source: Let Us Do (measuring turns), Q1

items.question: Guess the measures of each of the angles shown below. Then, check using your angle measuring tools. You may need to use a combination of measures. Also, state whether each of the angles is acute, right, or obtuse.
steps: The pieces are 1/8, 2/8 (a 1/4), 1/6, 2/6 (a 1/3) and 1/12. Lay them side by side on each angle.
Angle 1: the narrowest, about one 1/12 piece: about a 1/12 turn. It is less than 1/4, so acute.
Angle 2: one 1/6 piece: a 1/6 turn. Acute.
Angle 3: one 1/8 piece: a 1/8 turn. Acute.
Angle 4: about one 1/6 piece: about a 1/6 turn. Acute.
Angle 5: one 2/8 piece: 2/8 = 1/4, a right angle.
Angle 6: about one 2/6 piece: about 2/6 = 1/3, more than 1/4 and less than 1/2, so obtuse.
Angle 7: a 1/8 piece and a 2/8 piece: 1/8 + 2/8 = 3/8, more than 1/4 and less than 1/2, so obtuse.
Check: 1/12, 1/6, 1/8 and 1/6 are each less than 1/4, so those four are acute.
items.answer: 1: about 1/12, acute; 2: 1/6, acute; 3: 1/8, acute; 4: about 1/6, acute; 5: 1/4, right; 6: about 1/3, obtuse; 7: 3/8, obtuse.

videos.answer: 1: about 1/12, acute; 2: 1/6, acute; 3: 1/8, acute; 4: about 1/6, acute; 5: 1/4, right; 6: about 1/3, obtuse; 7: 3/8, obtuse.

source: Let Us Do (measuring turns), Q2

items.question: Guess the measure of the turns made by the arrow in each of the following cases. Verify with a combination of angle measuring tools. (a): 1/4 + 1/8 turn or 3/8 turn (this part is already solved in your maths book); (b): ___ turn; (c): ___ turn; (d): ___ turn
steps: The arrow turns from a starting arrow to an end arrow, the way the hands of a clock move.
(a): your maths book gives 1/4 + 1/8 = 2/8 + 1/8 = 3/8 turn.
(b): from straight up round to the lower left. It passes a half turn at straight down and goes 1/8 more: 1/2 + 1/8 = 4/8 + 1/8 = 5/8 turn.
(c): from straight up to the upper right: half of a quarter turn, a 1/8 turn.
(d): from the upper right, 1/8 of a turn from straight up, to a little left of straight down. Lay a 1/4 piece and a 1/6 piece: about 1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12 turn.
Check: (d): is a guess. 5/12 is more than 1/3 and less than 1/2, which matches an arrow that stops a little short of a half turn.

source: Let Us Do (measuring turns), Q3

items.question: Measure each angle in the given shapes. Write the measure of the angles in terms of turns and describe whether they are acute, obtuse or right angles. (a): the lines AB and A'B' cross at C and B'A joins B' and A; angles marked at B' and A. (b): the four-sided shape D, E, D', E'; angles marked at D, E and D'. (c): the four-sided shape F, G, F', G'; angles marked at F, G and F'.
steps: Lay the pieces on each marked angle.
(a): the angles at B' and A are each one 1/8 piece: a 1/8 turn each. Acute.
(b): the angles at D and D' are each one 1/6 piece: a 1/6 turn. Acute. The angle at E is two 1/6 pieces, a 2/6 piece: 2/6 = 1/3. It is more than 1/4 and less than 1/2: obtuse.
(c): the angle at F is a 1/8 piece: acute. The angle at G is a 2/6 piece: 1/3, obtuse. The angle at F' is a 2/8 piece: 2/8 = 1/4, a right angle.
Check: the angles in (a) and at F are the same size, and G is the same size as E.
items.answer: (a): B' and A are 1/8, acute; (b): D, D' are 1/6, acute, E is 1/3, obtuse; (c): F is 1/8, acute, G is 1/3, obtuse, F' is 1/4, right.

videos.answer: (a): B' and A are 1/8, acute; (b): D, D' are 1/6, acute, E is 1/3, obtuse; (c): F is 1/8, acute, G is 1/3, obtuse, F' is 1/4, right.

source: Draw an angle of a 1/2 + 1/12 turn on a given line. What kin

items.question: Draw an angle of a 1/2 + 1/12 turn on a given line. What kind of angle is it?
steps: Turn the line a half turn, then 1/12 more, in the same direction.
A half turn is 6/12, and 7/12 is more than 6/12.
So the angle is more than a half turn: more than a straight angle.
Draw the second line along the edge of the 1/12 piece.
Check: 7 pieces of 1/12 are one piece more than the half turn of 6 pieces.
items.answer: A 7/12 turn, more than a straight angle

videos.answer: A 7/12 turn, more than a straight angle

source: Let Us Do (measuring turns), Q4

items.question: Draw angles for the given measures of turns using the given lines.
steps: Take one end of each line as the corner of the angle. Turn the line by the given part of a full turn and draw the second line.
1/2 turn (vertical line): a half turn. The second line goes the opposite way, so both lines lie in one straight line: a straight angle.
1/4 turn (slanting line): a quarter turn, a square corner. The second line makes a right angle with the first. Use the 2/8 piece.
1/8 turn (vertical line): half of a quarter turn, a narrow acute angle, half of a square corner. Use the 1/8 piece.
1/12 turn (slanting line): half of a 1/6 turn, a very narrow acute angle. Use the 1/12 piece.
1/4 turn (horizontal line): a quarter turn again, a right angle.
Check: the 1/8 angle is half of a right angle, and the 1/12 angle is narrower still.
items.answer: Sample answer: 1/2: a straight line; 1/4: a square corner, both times; 1/8: half a square corner; 1/12: narrower still. Your drawing may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: 1/2: a straight line; 1/4: a square corner, both times; 1/8: half a square corner; 1/12: narrower still. Your drawing may differ.

source: Let Us Do (measuring turns), Q5

items.question: Draw the angles formed by the following turns in your notebook. 1/2 turn, 1/4 turn, 2/4 turn, 1/6 turn, 4/6 turn, 3/12 turn, 1/2 + 1/4 turn, and 1/8 + 1/6 turn.
steps: Draw each angle from a line. Turn the line the given part of a full turn.
1/2 turn: a straight angle.
1/4 turn: a right angle.
2/4 turn: 2/4 = 1/2, so it is a straight angle.
1/6 turn: less than a 1/4 turn, so it is an acute angle.
4/6 turn: 4/6 is more than 3/6, and 3/6 is 1/2. So it is more than a straight angle.
3/12 turn: 3/12 = 1/4, a right angle.
1/2 + 1/4 turn: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4, more than 1/2: more than a straight angle.

1/8 + 1/6 turn: 1/6 is more than 1/8, so the total is more than 1/8 + 1/8 = 2/8 = 1/4. Each part is less than 1/4, so the total is less than 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2. It is more than 1/4 and less than 1/2: an obtuse angle.
Check: 2/4 and 1/2 are the same turn, and 3/12 and 1/4 are the same turn.
items.answer: 1/2 and 2/4: straight; 1/4 and 3/12: right; 1/6: acute; 4/6 and 1/2 + 1/4: more than straight; 1/8 + 1/6: obtuse.

videos.answer: 1/2 and 2/4: straight; 1/4 and 3/12: right; 1/6: acute; 4/6 and 1/2 + 1/4: more than straight; 1/8 + 1/6: obtuse.

source: The minute hand starts at the number 2 and moves 25 minutes.

items.question: The minute hand starts at the number 2 and moves 25 minutes. What turn does it make, and where does it stop?
steps: The hand starts at 2, which is the 10 minute mark, because 2 × 5 = 10.
A 1/12 turn is 5 minutes. 25 minutes is 25 ÷ 5 = 5 of these.
So the turn is 5/12 of a full turn.
The hand stops at the 10 + 25 = 35 minute mark.
35 ÷ 5 = 7, so the hand stops at the number 7.
Check: from 2 to 7 is 5 numbers, and each step from one number to the next is a 1/12 turn, so the turn is 5/12.
items.answer: A 5/12 turn; the hand stops at 7

videos.answer: A 5/12 turn; the hand stops at 7

items.question: Guess the measure of turns the minute hand of a clock makes in each of the following cases. The initial position of the minute hand is given. Draw the final position of the minute hand on the clock face. Discuss your reasoning in class. (a): When the minute hand moves by 15 minutes, it has made a ___ turn of the circle. (b): When the minute hand moves by 30 minutes, it has made a ___ turn of the circle. (c): When the minute hand moves by 45 minutes, it has made a ___ turn of the circle. (d): When the minute hand has turned by 1/12 of a full turn, it has moved by ___ minutes. (e): When the minute hand has turned a full-circle, it has moved by ___ minutes. (f): When the minute hand has turned by 1/6 of a full turn, it has moved by ___ minutes. (g): When the minute hand has turned by 4/12 of a full turn, it has moved by ___ minutes.
steps: A full turn of the minute hand is 60 minutes. A 1/12 turn is 5 minutes.
(a): 15 minutes: 15 × 4 = 60, so it is a 1/4 turn. The hand starts at 3 and stops at 6.
(b): 30 minutes: 30 × 2 = 60, so it is a 1/2 turn. From 6 the hand stops at 12.
(c): 45 minutes: 3 × 15 = 45, so it is 3 quarter turns, a 3/4 turn. From 9 the hand stops at 6.
(d): a 1/12 turn is 60 ÷ 12 = 5 minutes. From 1 the hand stops at 2.
(e): a full circle is 60 minutes. The hand starts and stops at 12.
(f): a 1/6 turn is 60 ÷ 6 = 10 minutes. From 2 the hand stops at 4.
(g): a 4/12 turn is 4 × 5 = 20 minutes, because one 1/12 turn is 60 ÷ 12 = 5 minutes. From 4 the hand stops at 8.
Check: 4/12 is the same as 1/3, and 20 × 3 = 60.

items.question: An arrow points down. It makes a quarter turn and now points left. Is the turn clockwise or anti-clockwise?
steps: Think of the arrow as a clock hand pointing at 6, straight down.
Left is the 9 on a clock.
A clock hand goes from 6 to 7, 8 and 9. That is the way a clock moves.
So the turn is clockwise.
Check: the other way from 6 is 5, 4 and 3, which points right, not left.
items.answer: Clockwise

videos.answer: Clockwise

source: Padma faces West and turns 3 right angles anti-clockwise. Wh

items.question: Padma faces West and turns 3 right angles anti-clockwise. Which direction does she face?
steps: Anti-clockwise from West, the order is West, South, East, North.
1 right angle anti-clockwise: South.
2 right angles: East.
3 right angles: North.
So she faces North.
Check: 3 right angles anti-clockwise is the same as 1 right angle clockwise, because 3 + 1 = 4. West turned 1 right angle clockwise is North.
items.answer: North

videos.answer: North

source: Which Direction: four creatures

items.question: The creatures below have made a quarter turn once. Tick the direction in which they have moved. (a): ladybug (Clockwise/Anti-clockwise); (b): snail (Clockwise/Anti-clockwise); (c): bee (Clockwise/Anti-clockwise); (d): ant (Clockwise/Anti-clockwise)
steps: Clockwise is the way the hands of a clock move. Think of the creature's face as a clock hand.
(a): the ladybug faces left, the 9, then up, the 12. 9 to 12 is the way a clock moves: clockwise.
(b): the snail's head is down, the 6, then left, the 9. 6 to 9 is clockwise.
(c): the bee faces left, the 9, then down, the 6. 9 to 6 is against the clock: anti-clockwise.
(d): the ant faces up, the 12, then left, the 9. 12 to 9 is against the clock: anti-clockwise.
Check: each creature made 1 quarter turn, which is 3 numbers on the clock.
items.answer: (a): clockwise; (b): clockwise; (c): anti-clockwise; (d): anti-clockwise.

videos.answer: (a): clockwise; (b): clockwise; (c): anti-clockwise; (d): anti-clockwise.

source: Which Direction: tap, lid and nut

items.question: Observe the direction of movement while opening a tap, unscrewing a lid or loosening a nut. Do they move clockwise or anti-clockwise?
steps: Turn a real tap, lid or nut the way it opens, and watch which way it goes.
To open a tap, unscrew a lid or loosen a nut, the usual turn is anti-clockwise.
To close a tap, screw on a lid or tighten a nut, the usual turn is clockwise.
Check: opening and closing are opposite turns, so one is clockwise and the other is anti-clockwise.
items.answer: Sample answer: usually anti-clockwise for all three. Your tap may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: usually anti-clockwise for all three. Your tap may differ.

source: Fun with Turns: Q1

items.question: The children in a class are playing a game in which the teacher tells them the direction in which they should rotate. Complete the table by filling the direction the children will face on completing the given turns. The starting direction is given in the table. (a): North, two right angles clockwise; (b): South, two right angles anti-clockwise; (c): East, four right angles anti-clockwise; (d): West, four right angles clockwise; (e): North, 5 right angles clockwise; (f): South, 3 right angles clockwise, 1/2 right angle clockwise, 1/2 right angle clockwise; (g): West, ___ right angles clockwise, four 1/2 right angles anti-clockwise
steps: The directions go clockwise: North, East, South, West. A right angle is a quarter turn, one step.
(a): North, 2 right angles clockwise: East, then South. It ends at South.
(b): South, 2 right angles anti-clockwise: East, then North. It ends at North.
(c): East, 4 right angles anti-clockwise: a full turn, back at East.
(d): West, 4 right angles clockwise: a full turn, back at West.
(e): North, 5 right angles clockwise: 4 of them are a full turn, and 5 − 4 = 1 more takes it to East.
(f): South, 3 + 1/2 + 1/2 = 4 right angles clockwise: a full turn, back at South.

(g): West. Four 1/2 right angles are 2 right angles anti-clockwise. The number before 'right angles clockwise' is not printed in your maths book. The end is West turned that number minus 2 right angles clockwise. Sample: if it is 3, then 3 − 2 = 1 right angle clockwise, and West ends at North.
Check: (c), (d) and (f) are full turns, so they end where they started.
items.answer: (a): South; (b): North; (c): East; (d): West; (e): East; (f): South; (g): the number is not printed; if it is 3, North.

videos.answer: (a): South; (b): North; (c): East; (d): West; (e): East; (f): South; (g): the number is not printed; if it is 3, North.

source: Fun with Turns: Q2

items.question: Padma is facing the toy shop. What place will she face if she takes a half turn clockwise?
steps: A half turn is 2 quarter turns.
Padma faces the toy shop. On her right are the parking sign and the guard, on her left is the bookstall, and behind her is the ice cream cart.
Clockwise, the first quarter turn takes her to face the parking sign.
The second quarter turn takes her to face the ice cream cart.
Check: a half turn makes her face the opposite way from the toy shop, and the ice cream cart is behind her.
items.answer: The ice cream cart.

videos.answer: The ice cream cart.

source: Fun with Turns: Q2 another way

items.question: What other way can Padma turn to face the same place?
steps: A half turn anti-clockwise is also 2 quarter turns.
Anti-clockwise, the first quarter turn takes Padma to face the bookstall on her left.
The second quarter turn takes her to face the ice cream cart.
So a half turn either way ends at the ice cream cart.
Check: a half turn clockwise and a half turn anti-clockwise both make her face the opposite way.
items.answer: A half turn anti-clockwise, 2 quarter turns the other way.

videos.answer: A half turn anti-clockwise, 2 quarter turns the other way.
